text.label: Text: What A Funnel Hack Is
text.value: What A Funnel Hack Is

text.label: Heading: A funnel hack is me walking the same path your follower walk
text.value: A funnel hack is me walking the same path your follower walks.

text.label: Text: In plain words.
text.value: In plain words.

text.label: Text: A funnel is just the path a stranger takes from the first ti
text.value: A funnel is just the path a stranger takes from the first time they see you to the day they pay you. Every coach, author and influencer has one, whether they built it on purpose or not. A funnel hack is me walking that path the way a follower would, on screen, out loud, one step at a time. I tap what they tap and I read what they read. I am doing what your follower does and telling you what I see.

text.label: Text: The path I walk.
text.value: The path I walk.

text.label: Text: I start at a video, the same way a stranger does. Then I do
text.value: I start at a video, the same way a stranger does. Then I do what a curious person does next. I tap the profile and look for a link. I tap the link and see where it lands, and whose page that is. I look for something to buy. I look for a way to ask a question, and I look at what happens after somebody asks. I look for proof from people who have already been helped. Then I look at what happens to the follower who goes quiet, and whether anybody ever goes back for them. Each of those stops is a place where a follower either keeps going or gives up and scrolls on.

text.label: Text: Why you can't see yours.
text.value: Why you can't see yours.

text.label: Text: You cannot see your own path. You built it, so you know wher
text.value: You cannot see your own path. You built it, so you know where everything is. A stranger does not. They give you a few seconds, and if the next step is not obvious they are gone, and you never find out they were there. That is why watching somebody else's path get walked is so useful. You see the gaps in theirs fast. Then you go look at your own and find the same ones.

text.label: Text: Who owns each stop.
text.value: Who owns each stop.

text.label: Text: Most of the time the path never leaves social media. The vid
text.value: Most of the time the path never leaves social media. The video is on one platform. The link goes to a page of more links that belongs to another company. The sale, if there is one, happens in a private message. Not one of those stops belongs to the person who earned the attention. If that account were gone in the morning, they would have no way to tell a single follower where they went. So the first thing I look for is simple. Is there a website this person owns, and does the attention ever get there? And I do it with my own business, in front of you. The same thing I sell is the same thing I use. Show after show you watch me build it and run it, so you can see for yourself that I do what I tell you to do.

text.label: Pull line
text.value: You cannot see your own path. You built it, so you know where everything is.

text.label: Text: What You Will See
text.value: What You Will See

text.label: Heading: A big audience, and nothing to sell them.
text.value: A big audience, and nothing to sell them.

text.label: Text: The same mistake.
text.value: The same mistake.

text.label: Text: I see it with people who have 5,000 followers and with peopl
text.value: I see it with people who have 5,000 followers and with people who have 50,000. They worked for years to earn the attention. Then you go looking for what they sell and there is nothing there. No book. No program. No page with a price on it. Sometimes there is a link to a list of more links. That is a crowd clapping for somebody who never passes the hat. They did the first half of the business better than almost anybody. Nobody ever showed them the second half.

text.label: Text: Or it all runs through them.
text.value: Or it all runs through them.

text.label: Text: The other one I see has something to sell, and it only sells
text.value: The other one I see has something to sell, and it only sells when they personally answer every message. They are the website, the salesperson and the follow up, all from one phone. It works until they get busy, get sick or go to sleep. Then the messages sit, the interest cools off, and the buyer goes to somebody who answered. On the show I point at the exact spot where that happens, so you can see it with your own eyes.

text.label: Text: What I check.
text.value: What I check.

text.label: Text: The first thing I check is the simplest. Is there something
text.value: The first thing I check is the simplest. Is there something to buy? If the answer is no, nothing after it matters yet, because there is nothing for the attention to turn into. Then I check six more things, in the same order every time, because they are the six systems in our Revenue Engine and that is the order we build them in. Is there a website they own? Does every video, clip and episode send people to it? Does a question get answered in seconds, or in days? Is there proof from the people they have helped? Does anybody go back to the followers who went quiet? Ads come last, and only once the free attention is already turning into buyers. A follower meets those stops in their own order. I keep score in ours.

text.label: Text: What you learn.
text.value: What you learn.

text.label: Text: Watch a handful of episodes and you start seeing it without
text.value: Watch a handful of episodes and you start seeing it without me. You learn why a follower needs to see you and hear from you seven to ten times before they pay, and what has to be in place to keep that up. You learn what a product is, and why your own e-book, with your name on the cover, is the first one. The reason is plain. A book is a small yes. A follower who is nowhere near ready for your program will still buy a book, and the day they do, they stop being a number on somebody else's platform and become a buyer you can reach again. And you learn to look at your own page and say out loud where the attention stops.

text.label: Text: Respect first.
text.value: Respect first.

text.label: Text: This is a show about people who are good at what they do. I
text.value: This is a show about people who are good at what they do. I walk real pages that anybody can pull up on a phone, the biggest names included, and I say whose they are. Pull one up and walk it along with me. Some of them are my favorite people to watch. Everybody I look at has done the hard half. They earned the attention, and most people never do. That is the whole reason the show exists. I have run five businesses over forty years, and the lesson was the same in every one. The talent was never the problem. The system behind it was. So I call it like I see it and I show what goes in the gap. A gap can be fixed, and every gap that gets closed is attention turning into dollars.

text.label: Text: What a talent agent sees.
text.value: What a talent agent sees.

text.label: Text: That is the job my team and I do, and it is why we call ours
text.value: That is the job my team and I do, and it is why we call ourselves a modern day talent agency. A good talent agent sits in the back of the room and watches the act the way the audience does. He sees the moment the crowd was ready to buy and nobody asked them. The talent cannot see that from the stage. Funnel Hack Live is that seat in the back of the room, every weekday. And when you are our client, we do not stop at pointing. We show you how to promote yourself, we package what you know, and then my team does the heavy end of the work for you, on a website you own, with a sales system behind it. That sales system is our proprietary Revenue Engine.
